correctness.rationale: The finite-signature reduction is mathematically sound. At each observed prefix, every reachable accepted span is generated by a subset of the observed elements, so only finitely many intersection-rank signatures occur even over an infinite field. Those signatures determine all subspace constraints in the acceptance LP. The modular-lattice uncrossing and chain-supported dual argument then give feasibility, after which the source paper's acceptance-probability calculation yields the \(1/e\) guarantee. The committed rational verifier correctly checks a finite sample of the signature invariance and 1,521 supermodularity inequalities, but the theorem is supported by the general argument rather than that finite sample.
residual_risks: The result is existential; no uniform efficient procedure for enumerating realized signatures over an arbitrary field encoding is provided.

originality.rationale: The claim is already mechanically implied by the motivating paper's own finitary-modular-extension proof. That paper states the online representation theorem only for finite fields, but in its later modular-extension argument it constructs the same online acceptance process in a fixed finitary modular extension, handles infinitely many flats by exactly the finite intersection-rank signature used here, uncrosses to chains, and completes the same feasibility proof. A fixed finite-dimensional vector space over any field is precisely such a finite-rank modular ambient geometry. Specializing that already-published construction to the vector-space lattice gives the audited arbitrary-field online theorem without a new mathematical ingredient.
residual_risks: The paper's theorem headline does not spell out this arbitrary-field online corollary; the originality failure is based on mathematical implication from its proof, not title matching.
